To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the adsorption of MPs for pollutants can be significantly enhanced in the presence of coexisting surfactants.
co-existing surfactant can enhance the adsorption capacities of MPs for ionic organic pollutants, and the effects are dominated by electrostatic interactions.
co-existing surfactant can significantly enhance the adsorption of hydrophilic pollutants by hydrophobic MPs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of surfactant co-existing on the adsorption behavior of MPs, which may be a new mechanism to enhance the capacity of MPs to adsorb ionic pollutants in the marine environment.
a new mechanism that can significantly increase the capacity of hydrophobic MPs for adsorbing hydrophilic pollutants and thus has important implications for the environmental behavior of MPs.
the influence of co-existed surfactants on hydrophilic pollutant adsorption by MPs, which may be of significance for the fate of MPs and the risk assessment of environmental MPs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the adsorption capacities of MPs for hydrophilic ionic organic pollutants are significantly enhanced by co-existing ionic surfactants, and this phenomenon should be considered in future studies of MP pollution.

the presence of coexisting surfactants could enhance the adsorption capacity of MPs for hydrophilic pollutants by 1–4 orders of magnitude, and this effect should be considered in future research on the interactions between MPs, surfactants, and organic pollutants in the marine environment.
the adsorption of hydrophilic pollutants by MPs can be enhanced significantly in surfactant-containing environments, which may lead to a higher risk of environmental and ecological impacts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
surfactant-activated MPs are more likely to be enriched by pollutants in natural waters.

the co-existing surfactant can enhance the adsorption capacities of MPs for ionic organic pollutants with opposite charges, while the surfactants with nonionic hydrophilic chains can impede the adsorption of the pollutants.
the adsorption of MPs to hydrophilic pollutants can be significantly enhanced by coexisting surfactants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MPs may become more effective sorbents for ionic pollutants in environments containing surfactants.
the adsorbed pollutants on the surface of MP particles may be significantly influenced by the co-existence of surfactants.
the presence of surfactants can significantly enhance the capacity for MPs to adsorb hydrophobic pollutants, and this effect should be considered in the assessment of the environmental risks of MPs.
